title: Competitor Map Analysis for Dealerships | GAS.net
text:
Competitor map analysis means looking at the dealerships and repair shops that appear in Google’s map results for your searches, and comparing their profiles with yours. Much of a Business Profile is public: its category, rating, review count, photos and hours. Set side by side, those details often show why one business appears and another does not.

Updated October 6, 2026

You do not choose your competitors on the map. Google does, one search at a time.

The dealer across town may never appear beside you, while a tire shop two blocks away shows up in every service search.

## How to think about it

1. ### Competitors change with the search.

Sales searches, service searches and parts searches each bring a different set of businesses.
2. ### They change with the location.

The three businesses shown downtown are not the three shown twenty miles out.
3. ### Most of what you need is public.

Anyone can see a profile’s category, rating, review count, photos, hours and links.
4. ### Some of it is not.

A competitor’s calls, clicks and direction requests are visible only to that profile’s owners and managers.

...

1. Choose three to five searches that matter, across sales and service.
2. Choose three to five places in your market to search from.
3. Use a phone in each place, or a grid rank tracking tool.

...

1. Write down the three map results for each search and place.
2. Count how often each business appears.
3. Note where you appear and where you do not.
3. Step 3

### Compare profiles

1. Open the profiles that appear most often.
2. Record category, rating, review count, the date of the newest review and the newest photo.
3. Put your own profile in the same table.

## What to compare

| Item | Where to see it | What it tells you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Category | On the profile, under the name | Whether they are matched to the search and you are not |
| Rating and review count | On the profile | How well known and well regarded they appear to Google |
| Newest review | Sort the reviews by newest | Whether customers are still being asked |
| Photos | The photos section | Whether the profile is being kept up |
| Department profiles | Search their name with the word service | Whether they have an entry in service searches. See service department GBP. |
| Distance from each search point | The map | How much of the result is simply location |
| Business name | On the profile | Whether words have been added against Google’s guidelines |

title: Local SEO Benchmarks for Car Dealers: 2026 Report | Flento
text:
#### The benchmark discipline

This report sets operational standards and a repeatable way to compare your dealership with relevant local peers. It combines official platform guidance with Flento’s industry recommendations. Benchmark here means a defined comparison method; the report does not claim observed global averages or an analysed sample of car dealers.

...

#### Platform requirements

Google documents profile eligibility, representation rules and performance definitions. These define what information belongs on the profile and how supported metrics should be interpreted.

#### Industry context

Google documents dealership, department and new-car brand profile arrangements. Used-car dealerships cannot create profiles for each vehicle brand. These representation rules are not observed sales benchmarks or a ranking-effect estimate.

#### Your comparison data

Use your own dealership records and a defined local-peer set to calculate a baseline. Flento’s scorecard, test plan and illustrative calculation are operating tools. They are not measured market findings.

...

#### The documented factors

Relevance concerns the match between the business and the search. Distance depends on the searcher’s location. Prominence concerns how well known the business is, including links and reviews. Google does not sell a better local ranking or publish precise algorithm weights.

#### Build the right segment

Segment car dealers by the actual operating model, customer need and service scope. Use dealerships with comparable new or used stock and franchise model as a starting point. Record meaningful differences before treating two locations as interchangeable. Make the actual offer understandable and the business information accurate. Compare observations under consistent conditions; a larger service area or a publishing schedule does not establish a guaranteed ranking improvement.

...

#### Choose useful proof

Useful evidence includes actual vehicles and clear stock and branch identification. Attribute examples accurately and retain permission where people, private premises or client work are involved. A photograph or credential should answer a customer question rather than imply a result the business cannot substantiate.

#### Check before publishing

For a real Business Profile, use photographs of the actual business, products or service. Check accuracy, permission and confidential details. The conceptual image in this report is editorial artwork, not a real customer location or evidence of an outcome.

...

### Compare businesses that answer the same need.

Flento method for defining a relevant comparison group.

#### Match the operating model

Select dealerships with comparable new or used stock and franchise model. Match geography, service mix, customer segment and fulfilment format. Record meaningful differences in availability or scope rather than ranking every business with a similar category against one undifferentiated average.

#### Record inclusion rules

Specify geography, service type, opening or contact model, language and eligible locations before collecting peer observations. Record why each dealership belongs in the set. Exclude duplicates and unrelated formats rather than adjusting the group after seeing the results.

### Collect the visible facts. Keep unknowns visible.

Flento worksheet for comparing your dealership with relevant local peers.

| Subject | Detail | Consideration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity and location | Name, address model and profile URL | Verify eligibility; do not infer ownership from a search result. |
| Service fit | Categories and publicly described offers | Record what is visible, not assumed capacity. |
| Customer proof | Review count, rating and useful imagery | Save collection conditions; these do not reveal completed sales. |
| Action path | Website, phone and supported booking links | Test the destination and record failures. |
| Visibility check | Query, location, language and observed placement | |
| | | Do not label an unobserved result as rank zero.

title: Complete GBP Optimization Guide for Car Dealerships — A3 Brands
text:
## The GBP setup checklist for dealerships

Most dealers claimed their profile years ago and never went back. Here's what a properly configured dealership GBP looks like.

Primary category: get this right. Your primary category is the single strongest ranking signal for map pack visibility, according to Whitespark's 2023 Local Search Ranking Factors study. For most dealers:

- ● New and used: "New Car Dealer"
- ● Used only: "Used Car Dealer"
- ● Service-focused: "Auto Repair Shop"

Pick the one that matches your primary revenue. Don't guess. This one field affects every local search you appear in.

Secondary categories: add all that apply. Google allows up to 10 categories. Dealerships should use them. Common secondary categories:

- ● Used Car Dealer (if primary is New)
- ● Auto Repair Shop
- ● Oil Change Service
- ● Tire Shop
- ● Auto Parts Store
- ● Car Leasing Service
- ● Truck Dealer (if applicable)

Every relevant category you add expands the queries where your profile can appear.

...

## Photos and videos that actually help rankings

Google has confirmed that businesses with photos receive 42% more requests for directions and 35% more click-throughs to websites compared to those without (Google, 2024). For dealerships, photos do two things: they signal to Google that your profile is active, and they signal to buyers that your store is real.

### What to upload:

- ● Exterior shots. Front of dealership. Signage clearly visible. Multiple angles. This is what buyers look for when driving to your store.
- ● Interior shots. Showroom floor. Waiting area. Finance office. Buyers want to know what they're walking into.
- ● Team photos. Sales team. Service advisors. Your GM. Real people make the profile feel human. Stock photos do the opposite.
- ● Inventory highlights. New arrivals. Featured models. Special editions. This isn't about selling a specific car, it's about showing Google and buyers that your lot is stocked and active.
- ● Service bays. Lifts, equipment, clean shop floor. Fixed ops searches are high-intent and high-margin. Show the facility.

### Frequency matters.

Upload at least 5 new photos per week. Google tracks upload frequency as an engagement signal. A profile that gets new photos weekly signals an active, operating business. A profile with no uploads in 6 months looks abandoned, because from Google's perspective, it might be.

### Videos work too.

Short walkarounds of new inventory. Service department tours. Quick GM introductions. Keep them under 30 seconds. Google Business Profile supports video uploads directly.

...

## Attributes and services checklist

Google gives you two tools most dealers ignore: attributes and services. Both expand the searches where your profile appears.

Attributes are binary markers, yes/no signals about your business. Google uses them to filter search results. When a buyer searches "wheelchair accessible dealership" or "dealership with Wi-Fi," Google checks attributes.

Mark every applicable attribute:

- ● Wheelchair accessible
- ● Wi-Fi available
- ● Restroom available
- ● LGBTQ+ friendly
- ● Women-led (if applicable)
- ● Veteran-led (if applicable)
- ● Identifies as Black-owned / Latino-owned (if applicable)
- ● Appointment required / Walk-ins welcome
- ● Online estimates available

Every checked attribute is a potential search filter match.

Services let you list specific offerings. For dealerships, this means listing every service your shop performs:

- ● Oil change (conventional and synthetic)
- ● Tire rotation
- ● Tire balancing
- ● Wheel alignment
- ● Brake inspection and repair
- ● Battery testing and replacement
- ● State inspection
- ● Emissions testing
- ● Transmission service
- ● Coolant flush
- ● Air conditioning service
- ● Recall repairs
- ● Factory-scheduled maintenance
- ● Detailing

List all of them. Each service you add is a keyword signal to Google. When someone searches "tire rotation near me," Google checks which businesses in the area have "tire rotation" listed as a service. If you didn't add it, you're not in the running.

title: Google Business Profile for Dealerships: Full Guide
text:
### Choose One Specific Primary Category

Your primary category is the single highest-impact setting on the entire profile. It is the field Google leans on most when deciding which local searches your dealership is eligible to appear in, and it carries far more ranking weight than any secondary category you add.

Select categories that complete the sentence “this business is a,” not “this business has a,” and never use categories purely as keywords.

Set “Used car dealer” as your primary, adding secondaries such as “Car finance and loan company” only where they genuinely apply. Treat the primary as a settled decision. Changing it can unsettle your ranking for weeks while Google re-evaluates which searches your listing belongs in.

In a Whitespark analysis of 1.8 million profiles, businesses with a specific primary category appeared in the top 10 local results 12.5% of the time, against 9.2% for those on a generic category, roughly a 36% higher rate.

“Used car dealer” set as primary, with genuinely applicable secondaries beneath it.

Here are the best Google Business Profile categories for a car dealership.

Google Business Profile categories for car dealerships, from Google’s category list (September 2026).

| Category | When it should be your primary | When it’s a secondary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Used car dealer | Your core business is selling pre-owned vehicles to retail buyers | You are a new-car franchise dealer whose primary reflects the brand or “Car dealer,” but you also sell used inventory |
| Car dealer | You sell both new and used inventory and no narrower term fits | You sell used primarily but want to remain eligible for broader “car dealer” searches |
| Truck dealer | Trucks are the majority of what you stock and sell | You carry trucks alongside cars, but they are not the core of the business |
| Car leasing service | Leasing is your primary transaction model rather than outright sales | You offer lease options, but most volume is financed or cash purchases |
| Car finance and loan company | Financing is a standalone business, not a dealership add-on | You provide in-house or arranged financing on the vehicles you sell |
| Car accessories store | Selling parts and accessories is your core retail business rather than vehicles | You stock accessories alongside sales |
| Car repair and maintenance service | Repair and maintenance is your main business rather than sales | You run a service function, better placed on a separate service profile than as a secondary on your sales profile |

...

### Dealership Photos: What to Upload and How Often

Shoppers judge a used car by its appearance before they call, so your photo library does real conversion work. Upload real shots of your actual lot and cars, not stock or manufacturer press images. Add fresh photos every month, since recency signals an active listing.

Cover the categories buyers and Google both look for:

- Exterior storefront, so shoppers recognise you on arrival
- Lot inventory as it actually stands this month
- Interior showroom
- Your finance office
- Staff on the floor
- Customer delivery moments

All photos should follow Google’s business photo guidelines.

Birdeye’s 2025 State of Google Business Profiles analysis reports that profiles with 15 or more photos consistently saw stronger engagement in clicks, calls, and directions requests. That is a correlation across profiles rather than proof that photos cause calls, but the direction is consistent.

...

### Q and A: The Shift to Ask Maps

This surface is changing. Google retired the Q&A API in late 2025 and is moving to an “Ask Maps” model that generates answers from your profile details, reviews, website, and posts. The move is to feed those sources rather than maintain a manual FAQ box. Keep your description, services, attributes, and hours complete, since that is what Google now answers from.
author: Sam Daaz

title: Car Dealership Local SEO: Sales, Service & Parts Playbook
text:
Local SEO for a car dealership is the discipline of making one physical store visible and credible across Google Search and Maps for three distinct businesses: vehicle sales, service, and parts. Each profit center answers different queries, carries different margins, and converts on different urgency.

Google's local ranking guidance says local results rest mainly on relevance, distance, and prominence, and that there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. Complete and accurate profile information, review responses, photos, and in-store products all support visibility. Those inputs play out on two surfaces for a dealership: the map pack, which your Business Profile drives, and localized organic results, which your website drives. Our local ranking factors guide explains the generic mechanics; this page deals in what they mean for a store with three P&Ls.

| Profit center | Typical query shape | Urgency profile | What a conversion looks like |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vehicle sales (variable ops) | brand + city, "car dealer near me," model and trim research | Weeks of research, then sudden | Test drive booked, vehicle delivered |
| Service (fixed ops) | "brake service," "oil change near me," recall and warranty work | Same-day to same-week | Service slot booked, repair order closed |
| Parts | "[brand] parts counter," accessories, wholesale accounts | Transactional, often same-day | Counter sale or fulfilled order |

...

Google's representation guidelines require a profile to represent the real-world business accurately, and departments follow the same rules. For a dealership the recurring snag is a name problem: the DMS record carries the legal entity, the signage carries the trade name, and the profile splits the difference. Pick the real-world name customers see and keep it identical across license, signage, profile, and site.

Category rules matter as much as the name. Google's category guidance says to choose the primary category that best describes the business, use additional categories for special departments and services rather than every product line, give independent public-facing departments their own profiles, expect category edits to sometimes trigger re-verification, and remember that custom categories cannot be created. In practice, a franchised store usually fits the brand-specific dealer category where one exists, and a used-only independent usually fits the used car dealer category. The full category decision lives in our dealer GBP categories guide, and setup lives in the dealer GBP guide. This page makes only the architecture decision.

...

| Verify | The rule behind it | Where the full fix lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Representation and eligibility: profile name, address, and departments match the real-world store | Google's representation guidelines | Dealer GBP guide |
| Category evidence: primary category best describes the whole business; additional categories only for genuine departments | Google's category guidance; edits may trigger re-verification | Dealer categories guide |
| Vehicle listings: confirm whether your account, location, and inventory source qualify to manage listings on the profile | Google's vehicle listings documentation | Dealer GBP guide |
| Review process: ask genuine customers, never incentivize, protect reviewer privacy in public replies | Google's review guidance | Review management guide |
| Completeness: accurate hours, departments, photos, and in-store products | Google's local ranking guidance: complete and accurate info supports visibility | Dealer GBP guide |
| Posts cadence: offers and events current, each with an expiry date | Advertising compliance plus store policy | Local SEO module (GBP posts, review replies, citations, rank tracking) |
author: Akshay VR
